title: How Lily Stole Christmas
cn: 第33集 · 莉莉怎么偷走了圣诞节
novel:
It was [[Christmas|Christmas]] in New York, and Ted was [[decorating|decorate]] the apartment with his [[favorite|favor]] [[ornaments|ornament]] — including a beautiful [[handmade|handmade]] one Lily had given him years ago. But when Lily saw it, her face went [[pale|pale]].

"That [[ornament|ornament]] was a gift from me," she said, her voice [[shaking|shake]]. "I [[gave|give]] it to you..."

"I know," Ted said. "It's my favorite."

"...after I [[called|call]] you a [[grinch|grinch]] for not putting up decorations," Lily finished. Then everyone [[froze|freeze]]. Because that was not what happened. What really happened was that Ted had [[answered|answer]] Lily's phone while she was in San Francisco, and she had left a [[voicemail|voicemail]] calling him a [[terrible|terrible]] name.

Ted had never told anyone. He had [[deleted|delete]] the message before Marshall could hear it. But Lily remembered. And now, standing in front of the Christmas tree, the [[truth|truth]] came out like an [[avalanche|avalanche]].

"You called me a —" Ted started.

"Don't," Lily said, tears in her eyes. "I was [[angry|anger]] and [[hurt|hurt]] and I took it out on you. I am so, so sorry."

Christmas was almost [[ruined|ruin]]. But Marshall, who had been quiet the whole time, picked up the ornament and hung it on the tree. "This is still beautiful," he said. "And so are both of you. Now can we please have [[eggnog|eggnog]]?"

Christmas.en: the Christian holiday celebrating the birth of Jesus on Dec 25

decorate.en: to make something look more attractive by adding things to it

favorite.en: liked more than all others of the same kind

ornament.en: a small object used to decorate something, especially a Christmas tree

handmade.en: made by a person, not by a machine

pale.en: (of skin) very light, especially from shock or illness

shake.en: to move quickly from side to side or up and down

grinch.cn: 扫兴的人；讨厌圣诞节的人
grinch.en: a person who dislikes Christmas and spoils others' fun

freeze.en: to stop moving suddenly, especially from shock or fear

answer.en: to reply; to pick up the phone

voicemail.en: a recorded message left after an unanswered phone call

delete.en: to remove something that was written or recorded

truth.en: the real facts about something; not a lie

avalanche.en: a large mass of snow falling down a mountain; a sudden flood of something

anger.en: a strong feeling of wanting to hurt or criticize someone

ruin.en: to damage something so badly that it cannot be used or enjoyed

eggnog.en: a sweet Christmas drink made from eggs, milk, and alcohol
